summary.headline: Mastek Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5% QoQ to INR 985 crore (1.8% cc), with 12-month backlog up 25% YoY to $310 million.
summary.overview: Revenue was $104.8 million, up 1.2% QoQ, with 15.4% operating EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 105.9 crore. Middle East disruption raised bench costs and delayed collections, weighing on margin, while UK and North America both grew sequentially. Management highlighted a $25 million, five-year AI transformation deal in North America and a 12-month backlog of $310 million. Top-5 and top-10 client revenue declined QoQ due to a timing gap on NHS England projects, and ESOP expense starts from Q2.

financial_highlights.change: +3.2% QoQ; +13.3% YoY in USD; +25% YoY in INR
After paying INR 107 crore variable pay

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Grew 3% QoQ in constant currency; EBIT near 20%. BFSI growth driven by FCA ramp-up, healthcare had a transition with NHS England old projects closing before new data modernization projects started.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew about 2% QoQ in constant currency and 6% in INR; backlog up 29.8% QoQ and 23.5% YoY. Large $25 million Salesforce Agentforce AI deal expected to ramp by H2 FY27.

segments.name: Middle East (AMEA)
segments.commentary: Faced severe headwinds from West Asia crisis, raising bench cost and delaying collections; some new orders signed late in quarter, but predictability low and ramp-up uncertain.

segments.name: Service line: Data, automation and AI
segments.commentary: Grew 9.8% QoQ, reinforcing AI transformation focus.

segments.name: Industry: Public sector
segments.commentary: Grew 7.9% QoQ, with UK local government new customer wins; policy changes after UK political change being monitored.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 performance to be better than FY26, but generally does not give formal guidance.
UK healthcare expected to ramp back from Q2 and H2; North America expected to become a growth engine by H2 FY27.
Middle East expected to stay flat at least, with return to growth if geopolitical stability improves.

ESOP grant from Q2 with estimated impact of $400,000 to $500,000 per quarter; Q2 margin to be hit by planned increments; no full-year margin guidance, with internal cost efficiencies aimed at mitigating a significant portion of impact.
North America to reach $28 million to $30 million quarterly run-rate before delivering mid-teens margins.
capex_capacity: North America needs scale of $28 million to $30 million quarterly revenue to deliver mid-teens margins; company is investing in sales and marketing there and plans further investment in healthcare and life sciences.
Headcount rose by 167 to 4,897 in Q1, with UK adding 125 on new project ramp-ups.

Internal business transformation: core systems (CRM, recruitment, payables) replaced with AI-native solutions; resources shifting to forward deployed engineers and forward deployed domain consultants, with a large portion of resources to become FDEs/FDDCs.
demand_pricing: 12-month backlog $310 million, up 3.2% QoQ; management said total order book (TCV) trends are also improving but does not disclose order book numbers.

40-plus AI-led new opportunities closed in Q1; large-deal pipeline increased across geographies; AI deals come from existing accounts (maturity model Level 0 to 5) and net new accounts linked to Oracle, Salesforce, Snowflake and Databricks.
Aggressive price competition on new wins and renewals; discounts generally around 15%, reaching 20-25% in one or two cases, not 50%.
Incumbent challenges on existing accounts and champion-challenger wins in new accounts are the key competitive headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: When will the FCA, Atlas and HADES deals and the US deal ramp up? Why did top-5 client revenue fall 4% QoQ and 12% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: FCA has started ramping and will ramp more in Q2; HADES is a renewal with steady revenue, not incremental; the North America deal ramps by H2 FY27. Top-client decline is a one-time timing gap as NHS England old projects closed before new data modernization projects began.

qa_highlights.question: How have TCV trends been, are discounts becoming irrational, and will healthcare return to sequential growth from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: TCV is moving in the right direction; the $25 million 5-year deal is an example. Discounts are around 15%, up to 20-25% in one or two cases, not 50%. UK healthcare expected to ramp from Q2 and into H2; US healthcare to ramp by H2, not firm for Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Excluding the $25 million US deal, the order book looks flat QoQ; how does the funnel look, when will Middle East deals ramp, and will US and Middle East margins stay suppressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Large-deal pipeline has grown across geographies. Middle East healthcare deal closed in Q1 with more close to signature; Middle East expected to stay flat at least. Margin pressure came from slower-than-expected ramp-ups causing bench cost and one-time collection slowdowns, expected to reverse later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Subcontracting cost trend and ESOP impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Subcontracting at 18.5% of revenue, in line with Q4. ESOP grant from Q2 with an impact of $400,000 to $500,000 per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What changed between Q4 and Q1 to make commentary more positive, and what was the EBITDA margin bridge Q4 to Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trajectory is similar to Q4, with more AI demand and execution of backlog from the last 3 to 4 quarters. Margin change reflected Middle East provisions for doubtful debts and unbilled amounts, mix change and UK regulatory costs, offset by cost efficiency and currency tailwind.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state EBITDA and EBIT margin given ESOP costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given; Q2 margin will be impacted by ESOP and increments; full-year impact to be mitigated significantly through internal cost efficiencies.

risks_watch: Middle East uncertainty from West Asia crisis: bench cost, delayed collections and provisioning; pipeline deal closures uncertain.
UK public sector budget and policy changes after political leadership change.
North America ramp-down of legacy projects must be offset before H2 turnaround.
Competitive pricing pressure and AI-led incumbent challenges on existing accounts.
Income tax assessment FY2022-23: INR 91 crore transfer pricing and INR 32.5 crore domestic income added; estimated tax impact about INR 31 crore; appeal filed 26 June.
DSO rose to 75 days; ESOP and Q2 increment costs will pressure margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI demand, UK healthcare and North America backlog, but cautious on Middle East and margins; management repeatedly flagged uncertainty and declined to give formal guidance.
key_quotes: Q1 has been a good quarter with predictable performance and growth.
Middle East business, on the other hand, continues to face some severe headwinds.
we are definitely seeing aggressive price competition, both in terms of net new wins as well as renewals that we are going through.
we believe we should be able to execute them at a much better margin than we see them today.

growth.why: Management says FY27 should be better than FY26 without numeric guidance, backed by a $310M 12-month backlog (+13% YoY USD), a $25M Salesforce AI deal ramping by H2 FY27 and North America targeting a $28-30M quarterly run-rate; utilisation fell 2% QoQ and Middle East is weak.
